newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia sells 182-day bills, sets new auction.
newsitem.headline: Croatia sells 182-day bills, sets new auction.

text.p: Croatia's Finance Ministry said it raised a planned 50 million kuna through 182-day treasury bills, first sold on Tuesday at a primary auction.
They are the government's longest maturity so far since it launched regular sales of 35-, 42-, 45- and 91-day T-bills last summer.
The interest was set at 11.25 percent with a single price of 94.688 percent.
Bid rates for the new bills ranged between 11 and 13 percent. Clients can view full auction details on page MFHT.
Almost the entire issue went to the banking sector with the share of non-banking investors at a meagre 0.0085 percent, the ministry said in a news release.

It announced the next auction for May 27, when 150 million kuna worth of 42-day bills will be offered. They were last issued at 9.50 percent last Tuesday. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
